title: Go SDK: stream-friendly typed structs and generic decode adapters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: provide ergonomic, production-safe Go helpers to decode structured outputs from Redwood streaming responses into strongly typed Go structs using generics. Deliver a small set of composable primitives: Decoder[T], StreamSink[T], and RetryEnvelope, plus examples illustrating full-response fallback and backpressure-aware streaming consumption. Motivation: customers build RLHF-style pipelines and product features that rely on structured JSON and function-calling outputs; current SDK surface requires boilerplate for incremental decode + error handling + retries. This ticket consolidates patterns, exposes a stable API for Go users (>=1.20), and includes tests, bench marks, and docs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Add Decoder[T] interface and 2-3 concrete implementations (JSONChunkDecoder, LineDelimitedDecoder, FallbackWholeResponseDecoder). 2) Provide StreamSink[T] that exposes a backpressure-friendly Next(ctx) iterator and a Subscribe(ctx) callback for push consumers. 3) Implement RetryEnvelope with idempotency metadata that integrates with existing client retry middleware. 4) Deliver end-to-end example: streaming chat -> decode function call args into typed struct -> on parse error fall back to full response decoding and surface a well-typed error. 5) Unit tests covering partial chunk errors, reassembly, goroutine-safety, and retry behavior. 6) Benchmarks showing no regression in latency for non-streaming flows and <= 8% throughput overhead for streaming decode compared to raw stream parsing.
design_decisions:
- Use Go generics for Decoder[T] so callers provide a target type rather than runtime reflection everywhere; constraint: any T must be unmarshallable via encoding/json or implement DecoderUnmarshal interface.
- Stream API surface: prefer a pull-based Next(ctx) to simplify backpressure and integration with existing context cancellation; also provide a Subscribe callback wrapper for event-driven clients.
- Fall back to whole-response decoding when streaming fails after N partial-chunk errors (configurable, default N=2) to avoid silent data loss.
- Keep internal buffers bounded (default 64KB) to avoid OOM when model emits large single tokens.
- Keep retry decisions outside the decoder: expose RetryEnvelope metadata so middleware can inspect method, idempotency-key, and last-successful-offset to perform incremental retries when the server supports resume semantics.
- Avoid introducing new reflection-heavy helpers to maintain minimal overhead and make go vet friendly.
implementation_notes:
- Add package: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/streamdecode with Decoder[T], adapters, and small helpers.
- Decoder[T] signature: type Decoder[T any] interface { Feed(chunk []byte) (maybe T, err error) ; Complete() (T, error) }. Implementations should return a sentinel ErrMoreData when partial.
- Provide combinators: RetryableDecoder[T], ValidationDecorator[T] that runs optional business validation functions and returns typed validation errors.
- StreamSink exposes: func (s *StreamSink[T]) Next(ctx context.Context) (T, error) and func (s *StreamSink[T]) Close() error. The iterator should return io.EOF when stream ends.
- Examples: chat_function_args.go shows type FunctionArgs struct { Action string `json:\"action\"`; Params map[string]string `json:\"params\"` } and the decoder wiring.
- Tests: use table-driven tests for chunk boundaries, unicode splits, nested JSON objects split across chunks, and error replay scenarios.
- Backpressure: implement internal token queue with capacity and block the underlying reader when queue is full; ensure Next respects ctx.Done() to cancel waiting goroutines.
- Compatibility: keep legacy UnmarshalStream helpers for two releases and mark deprecated in docs.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: generics add complexity for older code patterns. Mitigation: provide thin non-generic helpers and migration guide.
- Risk: decoding overhead may increase CPU/allocs. Mitigation: microbenchmarks and optimize hot paths (reuse buffers, avoid copies).
- Risk: subtle concurrency bugs. Mitigation: extensive race tests, CI stress test for 50 concurrent sinks.
- Risk: retry semantics mismatch across backends. Mitigation: RetryEnvelope is metadata-only; coordinate with runtime team to add resume tokens in protocol and feature-flag resume behavior.
comments: 2025-02-16 - Aisha: Initial ticket created after backlog grooming. Raised compatibility question about unmarshalling interfaces; decided to require either encoding/json or implement DecoderUnmarshal for custom types.

2025-02-20 - Marco: PoC complete for JSONChunkDecoder and simple Next iterator. Benchmarks show +3% allocs and ~2ms extra latency on 64-token streams; acceptable. Pushed branch feature/stream-decode-poc.

2025-02-24 - PR feedback from review@redwood: prefer context-first API (Next(ctx)) and avoid goroutine per subscriber for low-latency paths. Adjusted implementation to use single reader goroutine and channel multiplexing. See PR comment: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/3129#discussion_r987654.

2025-02-27 - QA: Found race when Close() is called concurrently with Next(); added mutex and additional tests. Also added bounded buffer to prevent OOM on large tokens.
